text:
Alex: heads up — apiserver in eu-central-1 is showing high watch reconnects and controller-manager leader flapping since ~03:20 after the GPU scale-up. pod scheduling delays too.
Dana: which pool? gpu-preempt or gpu-burst?
Alex: gpu-burst. we pushed a capacity run to meet a training job request. ~60 nodes came up in ~7m.
Zhi: seeing a pattern: node kubelet logs show repeated iptables-restore failures during attach. cluster-dns also got a GC spike around same time.
Carla: alert: infra-bot reports `apiserver.watch.errors > 3%` and `controller.manager.leader_changes > 1` at 03:23.
infra-bot: :warning: alert triggered (1727258888) — apiserver.watch.errors high in eu-central-1
Alex: logs snippet from kube-proxy on eucc-gpu-09:
```
iptables-restore: line 210: unexpected 'COMMIT'
kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```
Dana: conntrack table full -> SNAT packets dropped -> kube-apiserver traffic to cloud-metadata / VPC endpoints gets RSTs -> controllers can't reach cloud APIs for attach status -> leader election jitter.
Zhi: Cloud NAT metrics show SNAT exhaustion on the subnet; concurrent node attaches create many ephemeral connections for metadata, image pulls, and cert bootstrapping.
Carla: can we bounce kube-proxy on the most affected nodes? that usually flushes conntrack and reloads rules without a full node restart.
Alex: prepping a quick list of top nodes by `conntrack_count` and `iptables_errors`.
Dana: I'm throttling the autoscaler and switching to a serialized attach policy (maxConcurrency=4).
Zhi: did a soft restart of kube-proxy on 6 nodes — conntrack usage dropped ~40% within 30s. apiserver watch reconnects decreasing.
Carla: ✅ apiserver watch error rate down to baseline. leader election stable.
Alex: follow-up items: add autoscaler hook to check `node.conntrack_pct` before onboarding batch; add a synthetic SNAT exhaustion alert; increase conntrack max for gpu nodepool images where allowed by kernel; investigate why iptables-restore errors occurred (possible iptables version mismatch or race with CNI plugin).
Dana: I'll file INFRA-2054 and include timelines + `tcpdump` captures we took during the spike.
Zhi: note: dns GC spike looked correlated — kube-dns pods were doing heavy DNS churn from image registries. consider pre-warming image caches or staggering pulls.
Carla: runbook note: when encountering leader flaps during onboarding, check conntrack/NAT, kube-proxy iptables errors, and autoscaler parallelism before rolling back control-plane components.
Alex: good call. closing the thread — will follow up on the ticket and schedule a short postmortem.
infra-bot: incident resolved (1727258888) — mitigated at 03:30
Dana: adding owners for INFRA-2054: @dana, @zhi, @alex.
